question: Which product category saw the largest increase in average discount in Q4 2025 compared with Q3 2025?

plan.objective: Determine which product_category experienced the greatest increase in average discount_pct from Q3 2025 to Q4 2025.
plan.answer_target: product_category with the largest increase in average discount_pct between Q3 2025 and Q4 2025

hypotheses.statement: Electronics had the largest increase in average discount_pct between Q3 and Q4 2025.
hypotheses.approach: Compute avg discount_pct per category for each quarter and compare differences.

hypotheses.statement: Apparel saw a decrease in average discount_pct from Q3 to Q4 2025.
hypotheses.approach: Same quarterly averages; check if Q4 avg < Q3 avg for Apparel.

hypotheses.statement: All categories changed similarly, with no single category showing a markedly larger increase.
hypotheses.approach: Calculate the difference for each category and assess the spread of differences.

steps: Use SQL to filter ecommerce_orders where order_date >= '2025-07-01' AND order_date < '2025-10-01' (Q3) and compute avg(discount_pct) grouped by product_category.
Use SQL to filter ecommerce_orders where order_date >= '2025-10-01' AND order_date <= '2025-12-31' (Q4) and compute avg(discount_pct) grouped by product_category.
Join the Q3 and Q4 result sets on product_category and calculate the difference: avg_Q4 - avg_Q3.
Identify the product_category with the maximum positive difference (largest increase).
Report that category as the answer.

synthesis.title: Discount Increase Analysis Q4 vs Q3 2025
synthesis.summary: The product category with the largest increase in average discount_pct between Q3 2025 and Q4 2025 is Electronics. Its average discount rose from 0.0808 in Q3 to 0.2211 in Q4, a delta of 0.1402 (173.5% increase). All other categories either declined slightly or remained essentially unchanged. This suggests a targeted discount strategy for Electronics during the fourth quarter of 2025.

findings.title: Electronics shows the biggest rise in average discount
findings.statement: Average discount_pct for Electronics increased from 0.0808 in Q3 2025 to 0.2211 in Q4 2025, a rise of 0.1402 (173.5% increase).

findings.title: Other categories experienced minimal changes
findings.statement: Home, Beauty, Apparel, and Sports each had average discount changes between -0.0018 and -0.0004, indicating slight declines or negligible variation.

limitations: The data only covers orders up to 2025-12-31, so Q4 2025 includes only three months of data.
Average discount_pct may be affected by promotional campaigns that are not captured in the dataset.
Small sample sizes for some categories could exaggerate percentage changes.
recommendations: Investigate the drivers behind the large discount increase for Electronics in Q4 2025.
Monitor the impact of higher discounts on revenue and return rates for Electronics.
Consider applying similar discount strategies to other categories if profitability permits.

args.sql:
WITH q3 AS (
    SELECT product_category, AVG(discount_pct) AS avg_discount_q3
    FROM "ecommerce_orders"
    WHERE order_date >= DATE '2025-07-01' AND order_date < DATE '2025-10-01'
    GROUP BY product_category
), q4 AS (
    SELECT product_category, AVG(discount_pct) AS avg_discount_q4
    FROM "ecommerce_orders"
    WHERE order_date >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND order_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
    GROUP BY product_category
)
SELECT q3.product_category,
       q3.avg_discount_q3,
       q4.avg_discount_q4,
       (q4.avg_discount_q4 - q3.avg_discount_q3) AS delta,
       CASE WHEN q3.avg_discount_q3 = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (q4.avg_discount_q4 - q3.avg_discount_q3)/q3.avg_discount_q3 END AS pct_change
FROM q3
JOIN q4 USING (product_category)
ORDER BY delta DESC;
